title: Best Kids' Scooters UK
short: Six kids' scooters, from a toddler's first lean-to-steer scooter to a folding scooter for tweens, tested by parents and children over months.
intro: Kids' scooters range from stable three-wheelers for toddlers to two-wheeled folders for tweens, and the right one depends on age and size. This guide is based on Mumsnet's tested roundup (updated August 2026), where parents tested scooters with their children over a three-month period on school runs, parks, dog walks, and smooth and bumpy pavements, scoring ease of assembly, cleaning, transporting, storing and use. Only scooters with a named tester's hands-on review are included here, and prices are those quoted by Mumsnet (RRP or at time of writing). These are non-motorised children's scooters; helmets are a sensible idea for any scooter.

products.name: Mini Micro Deluxe
products.best_for: Toddlers and preschoolers aged 2 to 5 taking their first scoots
products.key_spec: Ages 2 to 5, 2kg, tilt-to-steer three wheels, LED wheels, max 35kg, five colours
products.summary: Mumsnet's Best Buy. Testers found it a joy to use day to day and a great option for the school run: it makes it easy for a small toddler to kick off and go, with a smooth, well-engineered lean-to-steer mechanism and a simple footbrake. It's lightweight enough for toddlers to lift, with chunky silicone grips and an anti-slip footplate. Mumsnet notes it's expensive for the short period of use and doesn't fold, though spare parts and maintenance support are available.
pros: Lightweight enough for toddlers to lift
Bright LED wheels in five colours
cons: Expensive, especially considering the period of use

products.name: Primo Foldable Scooter
products.best_for: Children aged 3+ who want a folding scooter with a beginner-friendly brake and steering lock
products.key_spec: Ages 3+, 3kg, three-level adjustable handlebar (to 77.5cm), folding, rear brake, LED wheels, max 50kg
products.summary: Tested by a Mumsnet editor, who found it quick and easy to assemble and very easy to raise the handlebars as the child grows. Bright, battery-free LED wheels flash red, green and blue and help visibility in poor weather, and there's an extra-long rear brake and a steering lock for younger riders. It folds for travel. It's heavier than some models and has a more childlike design than the pricier Micro Maxi Deluxe.
pros: Chunky rear brake and steering lock for beginners
cons: More child-like design than the slightly more expensive Micro Maxi Deluxe

products.name: Xtend Ride-On Plus Scooter
products.best_for: Parents who want one scooter to last from baby ride-on to around age 12
products.key_spec: Ages 3 to 12, 4.75kg, 4-in-1 ride-on and scooter, extendable footboard, LED wheels, folds
products.summary: Tested by a Mumsnet editor with a three-year-old, who found it stable and secure and loved the LED wheels. It starts as a parent-pushed ride-on, becomes a toddler ride-on with under-seat storage, then a full scooter with an extendable footboard. The three-year-old found it trickier to manoeuvre than her lightweight Mini Micro, and it's heavy to carry. Older children may quickly outgrow the three-wheel design.
pros: Folds for easy transport and storage
cons: Older children may quickly outgrow the three-wheel design

products.name: Maxi Micro Deluxe Foldable
products.best_for: Children aged 5 to about 12 who are ready to move up from a mini scooter
products.key_spec: Ages 5 to 12, 2.5kg, three wheels, adjustable handlebar, folds, rear brake, LED wheels, max 50kg
products.summary: Tested by Mumsnet parents. One editor's six-year-old was impressed by how easy it was to steer and the size and efficiency of the brake, and her four-year-old found it easier to control at speed than the Mini Micro. Mumsnet users praise its longevity, with the ability to hand down to younger siblings without significant wear. It costs a lot, but is built to last.
pros: Height adjustable handlebar that grows with your child
Folds down for carrying or storage
Durable, hardwearing and easy-to-use rear brake
products.search: Micro Scooters Maxi Micro Deluxe Foldable

products.name: Micro Sprite
products.best_for: Children aged 5 to 12 who prefer a bike-like two-wheel scooter
products.key_spec: Ages 5 to 12, 2.85kg, two wheels, one-click folding, 360 steering, kickstand, max 100kg
products.summary: Tested by a Mumsnet editor and a parent-tester whose son used it on the school run: it was quicker than walking and comes with a strap to carry over the shoulder or hook on buggy handles. It has a folding aluminium frame, height-adjustable handlebar and bike-like steering, with a kickstand. It glides well and corners with ease, but the small wheels can be bumpy on rougher terrain, and younger children may prefer a three-wheeler.
pros: 360 smart handlebar steers like a bike
cons: Younger children may prefer a three-wheeler's stability
Small wheels less suited to rough terrain

products.name: Mid 9 Scooter
products.best_for: Tall tweens and teens up to about 14 who have outgrown bright three-wheelers
products.key_spec: For heights of 1.25 to 1.75m, folding, front-wheel suspension, handlebar brake, mudguards, max 100kg
products.summary: Tested by a Mumsnet editor whose daughter graduated to it from a smaller Globber and would ride it in any weather. It has a grown-up folding design in subtle colours, front suspension for a smoother ride over bumps, an easy handlebar brake and mudguards. Some older children may prefer a stunt scooter.
pros: Front-wheel suspension for a smoother ride
cons: Some older children may prefer a stunt scooter

guide.q: What age is right for a first scooter?
guide.a: Three-wheelers with lean-to-steer suit children from about two, like the Mini Micro Deluxe (ages 2 to 5). Older children move to taller three-wheelers such as the Maxi Micro (5 to 12) or two-wheelers like the Micro Sprite, and tall tweens to something like the OXELO Mid 9.

Three wheels are more stable for younger riders learning balance, as Mumsnet found with the Mini and Maxi Micro. Two-wheelers like the Micro Sprite steer like a bike and suit older children, but their small wheels are bumpier on rough ground.

guide.q: Is it worth paying more for a Micro scooter?
guide.a: Mumsnet users report Micro scooters lasting for years and being passed down, and the brand offers spare parts and maintenance support. Cheaper models such as the Globber Primo (RRP £65) are still good, but are heavier and may not last as long.

Folding helps for travel, school runs and storage: the Globber Primo, Maxi Micro Deluxe Foldable, Micro Sprite, smarTrike Xtend and OXELO all fold. The Mini Micro doesn't fold, but at 2kg it's light enough for toddlers to carry themselves.
